events.title: She Wants Revenge
events.description:
Goldenvoice Presents
She Wants Revenge

Sunday, October 18 | ​The Regency Ballroom

She Wants Revenge, the dark-alternative duo who first exploded onto the scene with the 2005 hit, “Tear You Apart”, are back with a new song, festival appearances, a new lineup, and a massive global audience hungry for the 3rd wave gothic rock they ushered in 2up and down decades before.

For Justin Warfield and Adam Bravin, She Wants Revenge began as a production duo making songs to DJ at clubs. But when a 3-song demo was passed to a friend, they signed to Geffen records, and soon the songs became the basis of their 2005 self-titled LP. They hit the road supporting Bloc Party, The Kills, and OKGO, and along the way, “Tear You Apart” became a bona fide hit. Soon they were opening for Depeche Mode, The Psychedelic Furs, Placebo, co-headlining with Peter Murphy of Bauhaus, headlining Coachella alongside Daft Punk, and in constant rotation on alternative rock across the country. In under a year the oddball tune they thought to be an evil cousin of the B52’s and Wall of Voodoo saw them blitzing through the late-night talk show circuit, and with singles “Out of Control”, and “These Things” also climbing the charts, they went on to sell over 300,000 albums.

Though they came to prominence in the mid-aughts post-punk revival, Justin and Adam were more indebted to their early influences; Prince, Tangerine Dream, ELO, Giorgio Moroder, and 90s hip-hop. It was their true to the era production style, thoug...

Join us for our monthly all-ages Queer Bowling event! Come and bowl for free while enjoying bites from local food pop ups, discounted drinks, DJs, and drag!

How it works:

+ Purchasing a ticket will guarantee you entry to the bowling alley. For every ticket sold we donate $10 to a local nonprofit of our choosing. In 2025 we raised $8k and supported the following organizations: Drag Story Hour, Mujeres Unidas y Activas, San Francisco AIDS Foundation, Vanguard Lab, Lyric Center for LGBTQQ+ Youth, SF Black Pride, Oaklash, Sí a la Vida, Bay Area American Indian Two-Spirits, & more!

You will also receive a complimentary drink ticket for the welcome drink (both alcoholic and non-alcoholic options available)

+ You will check-in with staff to place your name on the bowling list

+ When we are ready for you, you will be placed with your group or other guests to bowl on a lane

+ Bowling is FREE!

+ Each lane bowls for 5 frames (you have the opportunity to place your name back on the list to bowl again)

+ You will be able to order food or drinks from the bar

+ Bowling lanes are for bowlers ONLY. If you are waiting to bowl, you must wait in designated areas until your turn

+ Have fun!

This event is all ages.

events.title: Geese
events.description:
Another Planet Entertainment Presents
Getting Killed Again Tour
Geese
Monday, October 19 | Fox Theater

Ripping up the expected blueprint Geese set with their 2021 debut Projector and the cowboy rock follow-up of 2023’s 3D Country, Getting Killed puts the very idea of conventional rock structures in the band’s crosshairs. Working at a feverish clip with renowned producer Kenneth Blume over a month-long stretch, Geese emerged wielding a sharp, novel new vision for the genre, sporting wry smiles and a resolute confidence. The album was crowned the number one album of the year on numerous Best of 2025 lists including TIME, The New Yorker, The New York Times and more. The band began 2026 right where they left off, with an unwieldy, vexing SNL debut, a surprisingly intimate Tiny Desk concert and winning a BRIT Award for International Group of the Year.

events.title: Sewing 101: Hemming and Simple Repairs
events.description:
- Class Time: 7:00PM - 10:00PM

Keeping your wardrobe in good shape starts with learning a few basic repairs and alterations. Maybe you need to shorten a pair of pants with a new hem, fix a seam that has split open, or sew a button back on. In this beginner-friendly class, you will learn hand sewing techniques to keep your favorite clothes ready to wear!

Lessons covered in this class include:

- Hemming jeans, stretch fabrics, and delicate sheers

- Repairing seams

- Sewing on buttons

- Simple mending techniques

During class, you will practice using a selection of different fabrics. We also encourage you to bring a few items of your own to work on if you like. Your instructor will guide you through all hemming and repair techniques but will not directly mend your selected items. That's where you come in!! Each student will gain a working knowledge of each hemming and repair techniques, as well as the opportunity to work on 1-2 pieces from home.

Please Note: This is a beginner-friendly class that does not require prior hand or machine sewing knowledge. However, this would not be a replacement for one of our other Sewing 101 or Sewing Bootcamp classes, which give a more complete introduction to using sewing machines. Also, this class will not cover replacing / repairing zippers, as that's a whole 'nother thing!!

Supplies Needed: All materials for practice are provided so you can try out several techniques on different types of fabric. You may bring a few pieces from home...

events.title: Bebe Stockwell
events.description:
Another Planet Entertainment Presents
Bebe Stockwell
Monday, October 19 | ​Rickshaw Stop

Bebe Stockwell, the Boston-born singer, songwriter, and performer crafts folk anthems punctuated by an unapologetically and unfiltered Gen-Z perspective. Her life began in the neighborhood of Beacon Hill where she took piano, drum, and guitar lessons, and penning songs of her own served as an outlet as a kid. While attending the Clive Davis Institute of Recorded Music at New York University, she continued to write and record.

She eventually caught the attention of GRAMMY® Award-winning producer M-Phazes and together they collaborated on her 2022 breakout “Love Me Back,” which to date has amassed north of 7 million Spotify streams. “Love Me Back” paved the way for more music, including “Robbie,” “Frosty,” and “Helium,” as well as while along the way, she shared stages with the likes of Claire Rosinkranz, Stephen Sanchez, Rachel Chinouriri, and M. Ward in addition to gracing the bills of Newport Folk Festival and Boston Calling. In 2024, the songstress inked a deal with Columbia Records and she released her debut EP, Driving Backwards, to much acclaim in May 2025.

events.title: Author Talk: Ecofiction with Nina Schuyler and Holly Payne
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerThe Mill Valley Library presents a special conversation with award-winning author Nina Schuyler in honor of her inventive new ecological novel, Open the Floodgates.
In an unnamed California town, the River is granted personhood and has the right—and urgent need—to argue in court for its existence. But powerful, well-funded enemies are determined to keep the River exactly as it is: gunk-filled, toxic, a convenient dumping ground for waste. The story moves like water, entering the minds of the town’s people, pigeons, deer, dogs, cats, the trees, the River’s home, and the River itself. When the River is ultimately jailed, the town faces a reckoning: what do we owe the River? And the River must answer in turn: what, if anything, does it owe humans?

Nina Schuyler is the author of four other fiction books and teaches creative writing at Stanford Continuing Studies and the independent bookstore, Book Passage. Nina Schuyler’s newest short story collection, In this Ravishing World, won the PEN Oakland Josephine Miles Literary Award, the W.S. Porter Prize for Short Story Collections, and the Prism Prize for Climate Literature. It was also a finalist for the Northern California Book Award. She graduated from Stanford University with a B.A. in Economics and earned a law degree at UC Law San Francisco. She is also the author of How to Write Stunning Sentences and has an extensive following of her Substack newsletter of the same name.

events.title: Bobby Finger & Lindsey Weber – I Want to Be Famous
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerWhile being photographed in 1966, Warhol reportedly said, “Everyone wants to be famous.” (To which his photographer, Nat Finkelstein responded, “Yeah, for about fifteen minutes, Andy.”) But Warhol was right then, and he’s right now. Fifteen minutes be damned, all you need is the drive—or desperation—and a singular spark. But if you’re not careful, you’ll end up a Who.
Who is a Who? In I Want to Be Famous, Bobby Finger and Lindsey Weber, the pop culture journalists behind the podcast Who? Weekly, distill celebrity into two categories—Whos and Thems—transcending the snarky, antiquated judgment of the “A-Listers” to “D-listers.” If you come across an allegedly famous face you’ve never seen before and are compelled to utter “Who?”, well, there’s your answer (Can you picture Rita Ora, Ava Max, or Hilaria Baldwin without Googling them?). If the subject elicits something along the lines of, “Oh, Them,” there you’ve found the opposite (Beyoncé, Taylor Swift, Tom Cruise). It’s the fundamental duality of fame.

And yet, as more Whos spawn, the path to Themdom narrows. We’ve entered an era where accessibility to fame is within everyone’s grasp, though only a select few can crack the algorithm and hold our ever-diminishing attention spans. events.title: Yerba Buena Illuminated: Free 95-Ft Art Projection on Market Street
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerYerba Buena Illuminated: Free 95-Ft Art Projection on Market StreetSan Francisco has officially turned a downtown building into a giant art projector.

Yerba Buena Illuminated launched Tuesday, August 25, 2026 projecting giant digital artworks onto the historic Humboldt Bank Building at 785 Market St., at the top of Yerba Buena Lane. The massive projection covers a 95-foot-high by 46-foot-wide section of the building, turning one of Market Street’s historic facades into a giant outdoor art screen.

The free outdoor art show runs nightly from twilight until 10 p.m., with the first artwork on view for about 90 days. The inaugural projection is Jennifer Steinkamp’s It’s a nice day for a white wedding. (2008), from SFMOMA’s collection. Inspired by Billy Idol’s “White Wedding,” the digital artwork covers the Beaux-Arts-style building with a cascade of animated red, white and yellow wedding flowers.
The project is a collaboration between Yerba Buena Partnership, SFMOMA, the Museum of the African Diaspora and Yerba Buena Center for the Arts. And this first installation is just the beginning: MoAD and YBCA will curate future projections in 2027, so the giant building-as-canvas is sticking around.
The projection is designed to serve as a giant welcome sign for the Yerba Buena arts district, home to more than 60 public artworks and some of San Francisco’s biggest cultural institutions. The rotating projections will continue to light up the Humboldt Bank...

As an age-old tradition dating back to the early 1800s, Spanish travelers used “BOTA”, or traditional sheep-skinned repositories, to transport and share their wine. events.title: Queer Art Exhibition (SF Disability Cultural Center)
events.description: Submitted by the Event OrganizerIs art political? Of course, it is! From the brush strokes to the paint colors to the pen nib, everything is political! The real question is, are you courageous enough to follow these stories? You may not share their world view, but have you ever wondered what the world on the other side of your bubble believes in? This showcase highlights Queer tales that are often hidden from our platforms. They don’t fit these neat boxes. But they exist. Join me as I revisit these tales, actively dissent from the dominant narrative & engage with humans from across the spectrum.

events.title: Filmscreening: Punking Punk
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerPunk promised that anyone could get on a stage. It didn’t always keep the promise. These two documentaries follow the people who held it to its word: the women who founded the first all-female bands in Düsseldorf, West Berlin, and Zurich, and the queer punks who built a scene of their own when the movement’s macho turn pushed them out. Two films, one evening, and the same refusal to ask permission.
Einfach machen! She-Punks von 1977 bis heute
Reto Caduff, Germany/Switzerland 2024, 94 min, German with English subtitles

“Do it! Don’t talk about it. Do it!” Martina Weith, lead singer and saxophonist of Germany’s first all-female punk band Östro 430, summed up the movement’s radical practice in a single demand. Decades later, the women who led pioneering bands like Mania D, Malaria!, and Kleenex are back on stage, decrying patriarchy, sexual repression, dogmatic feminism, and right-wing violence with the same electric fervor. Caduff’s nervy documentary traces the story of the women of German-language punk — innovators and provocateurs who fought as hard against bourgeois society as against the subculture’s own machismo. With interviews from Weith, Gudrun Gut, and Bettina Köster, it looks back on punk’s contradictory gender dynamics and these women’s triumphant fight to plant their own black flag within it.
Queercore: How to Punk a Revolution
Yony Leyser, Germany/USA 2017, 83 min, in English
While some of punk’s brashest arms-bearers were enjoying...

events.title: Fruit Bats
events.description: Submitted by the Event OrganizerThe midwest, particularly the part of the midwest Eric D. Johnson hails from, is a largely flat expanse. Zipping through it on the highway, you’ll see cities and towns rise up in the distance, but blink and you’ll miss other man-made rejoinders to horizontal living dotting the landscape, hill after hill, built from the refuse of the past: landfills. Some of these hills make for great sledding spots, parks, and trails. Others turn organic waste into compost. The Landfill, Fruit Bats’ June 12, 2026 album from Merge Records, is something else entirely: a mountain dominating the landscape of Johnson’s heart.

events.title: Próxima Parada – Nico Solo Show
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerNico Larson is a California singer-songwriter and the lead singer, pianist, and guitarist of the band Próxima Parada. He writes vulnerable songs centered on personal growth and human connection.
Próxima Parada means “next stop” in Spanish and Portuguese. While riding the bus in their hometown of San Luis Obispo, California, Nico and his bandmates would hear at every stop, “Now approaching, próxima parada…” After years of touring the U.S. and moving from one next stop to another, the band has developed an uplifting, groove-driven sound that explores embracing who we are while working toward who we’re becoming. Their music blends elements of soul, R&B, folk, and indie rock.

For this solo performance, Nico will share Próxima Parada’s songs in their original form, just as he first wrote them: alone at the piano.

events.title: Free Parenting Workshop: Decode Your Child’s Behavior (Mill Valley)
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerBehind the Behavior: Understanding Your Child at Every Developmental Stage and What You Might See at Home
Friday, October 2, 2026
9:00-10:00 a.m. / Marin Horizon School Library
When we think about the beginning of the school year, we think about new teachers, new friends, new expectations, and all of the logistics of parenting a school-aged child. And then comes the push for more independence, the nightly meltdown that didn’t happen last year, or the “please don’t talk to me in front of my friends.” We may find ourselves wondering what happened and how did we get here? It’s easy to feel lost when our children enter a new developmental stage. We may understand what to expect from a parenting book or article, but it can be much harder to recognize and respond to these changes when they show up at home. In this workshop, we’ll explore the developmental stages of the elementary and middle school years, what to expect as children grow and change, and practical ways to navigate these new phases while strengthening communication, connection, and understanding with your child.

events.title: Carlos Motta: When Time Stands Still
events.venue: Institute of the Arts and Sciences
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerCarlos Motta’s When Time Stands Still, the artist’s second solo show with the IAS, features new and recent installations, videos, and sculptures highlighting the artist’s preoccupation with the historical and aesthetic productions of difference and marginalization that shape the present.
The selection of artworks in the exhibition explore the unsettling experience of living in a time that seems violently stuck on repeat. Archetypal figures from art history (a fool, a siren, a witness, a victim) reappear in the current moment as containers of time, bringing the past of imperialism, colonization, and displacement into a present marked by the rise of anti-immigration politics, climate injustice, and other forms of disposability. Some works challenge this violent repetition of time. The clock moves, if gruelingly, in an endurance-based video performance, No One, 2025. For forty-six minutes, the artist undertakes to keep his eyes open, witnessing, withstanding, confronting, and resisting the bombardment of images, both historical and otherwise, that normalize harm. In another video work, Gravity, 2024, performers enact rescue carries, supporting each other until they can’t bear the weight. Together, the artworks act as a proposal about how to rethink time—how to slow time—with a poetic and aesthetic cadence that might counter the numbing reverberations of living in the present.

Submitted by the Event OrganizerThe fifth annual Bay Area Maya Festival will be held on Saturday October 3, 2026, from 9AM to 1:30PM at City College of San Francisco’s Mission Campus, 1125 Valencia Street, between 22nd and 23rd Streets.
The Bay Area Maya Festival celebrates the living presence of the Maya community in the San Francisco Bay Area. The only event in the region to bring together Maya people across languages, regions, and traditions: Yucatec, Mam, Kʼicheʼ, Kaqchikel, and more.

The festival is a free, annual gathering for cultural celebration, community healing, and transnational exchange. Through music, dance, poetry, art, food, and workshops, we connect Maya families with their heritage and with one another, while inviting the broader community to learn from and stand alongside their Maya neighbors.
The theme for this year’s festival will be aj tz’ib, and is centered on Maya writers and writing in the largest sense of the words possible. Aj tz’ib intersects with many sub-themes: poetry, fiction, history, art, painting, weaving, pattern-making, the recording of and representation of knowledge, the preservation of the past, the imagining of the future. Submitted by the Event Organizer

This is Your City. This is Your Voice. This is Your Future. Share your story about growing up and raising your family in San Francisco.

Every family has a story. Every voice matters. Please share yours.

Through conversations with families across the city, we’re learning what matters most to children, youth, young adults, and families. What we learn will help improve future planning, programs, and services.
Whether you’ve lived in San Francisco your whole life or recently made it your home, your experiences and ideas matter.
District 5 Neighborhoods include: Tenderloin, Civic Center, Hayes Valley, Lower Haight, Western Addition, Fillmore, Alamo Square, Japantown, NoPA, and Haight Ashbury

events.title: Drawing From Film—Onibaba
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerWe’ll be pausing Shindō’s historical horror film, Onibaba, to draw striking frames.
Basic materials (pencils, paper, erasers) will be provided. You may bring your own materials, but please no fume-creating paint or paint pens. Watercolor, ink and gouache are fine.

This is a self-led event; there will be no instruction or feedback. However, there will be an opportunity at the end of the session to look at others’ drawings and show your own.
NR, 103 mins., 1964. Closed captions (CC) and subtitles in English. Due to pauses for drawing, the full film will not be shown.
The event takes places in the Main Library at 100 Larkin Street, in the Latino/Hispanic Meeting Room.

Submitted by the Event OrganizerCelebrating the grand opening of Hauser & Wirth Palo Alto and its inaugural exhibition, ‘Calder | O’Keeffe,’ please join us for an exhibition walkthrough with Calder Foundation President Alexander S. C. Rower and Senior Curatorial Director Alexis Lowry to discuss the artist Alexander Calder and his exceptional works on view.
Developed in close collaboration with the Calder Foundation, ‘Calder | O’Keeffe’ brings together works by these two iconic artists, complemented by archival materials documenting their decades-long friendship.

‘Calder | O’Keeffe’ is organized by Hauser & Wirth Curatorial Senior Director Alexis Lowry. The exhibition is our second major presentation of Calder’s work in California—the critically acclaimed exhibition ‘Calder: Nonspace’ was held at our downtown Los Angeles complex in 2018—and coincides with the upcoming presentation ‘Calder. François Premier’ opening at Hauser & Wirth Paris on 19 October 2026.
Following the walkthrough, join us for the Grand Opening on Emerson Street – a block party featuring live performances by Stanford Taiko and Cardinal Calypso, DJ sets by GULU, Tie Dye Trippin and bella d. and food trucks by Rincon Del Cielo Taqueria, Bay Area Munchiez and Crazy Empanadas. events.title: “The Tiny Monster Show” Free Art Exhibit + Halloween Costume Contest (Oakland)
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerWhether or not you like monsters, one has to admit, most of us like a good scare now and then. Curiously, the word Monster derives from the Latin “monstrum”, (divine omen, object of dread). In turn, “monstrum” is the derivative of “monere”, (to remind, warn, instruct, or foretell). From this vantage point, monsters take on a new inspiring role, not to just scare us, but to inform us. So what can monsters teach us about our fears, our society and beyond?The Tiny Monster Show explores our fears so we can take a deeper look at what we’ve been suppressing and what we need to confront.
From classical to political with a little humor in between, The Tiny Monster Show gives space to capture, reveal, and maybe conquer those elements that keep us frozen in fear and shine a light on what it means to be human. Perhaps you’ll experience a moment of laughter in recognition that you are more powerful than monsters would have you believe.

events.title: West Coast Wet Hop Harvest Fest (Oakland)
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerJoin us at Original Pattern Brewing for a brand-new celebration of fresh wet-hop beer, bringing together 30 breweries from up and down the West Coast for one incredible afternoon of freshly harvested hops, freshly brewed beer, live music, and local eats.
So, what makes wet-hop beer so special?

Unlike traditional dried hops, wet hops are harvested and brewed with fresh hops within hours of leaving the farm. Being just a short drive from some of the country’s best hop-growing regions gives West Coast brewers a unique opportunity to work with these incredibly fresh hops at the peak of their harvest.
The result? Beers that showcase the bright, vibrant, and uniquely fresh character of the hop in a way you simply can’t get from traditional dried hops. Brewing with wet hops is a rare opportunity, and we’re excited to bring together breweries from across the coast to celebrate this special part of the harvest season.
Expect a wide range of beers featuring fresh wet hops like Simcoe, Amarillo, Strata, Citra, and Mosaic, alongside plenty of other hop-forward creations.

events.description:
Submitted by the Event Organizer

Celebrating the grand opening of Hauser & Wirth Palo Alto and its inaugural exhibition, ‘Calder | O’Keeffe,’ please join us during our first day-long program of talks, readings, performances, books, music and food, for an exhibition walkthrough with Georgia O’Keeffe Director of Curatorial Affairs Dr. Laura Wertheim Joseph and distinguished scholar and professor of American culture at Stanford University, Alexander Nemerov to discuss the artist Georgia O’Keeffe and her exceptional works on view.
Developed in close collaboration with the Calder Foundation, ‘Calder | O’Keeffe’ brings together works by Alexander Calder and Georgia O’Keeffe, complemented by archival materials documenting their decades-long friendship.

Georgia O’Keeffe once remarked that she recognized her own ‘pelvis bone holes’ in Calder’s forms—a striking moment of artistic recognition that speaks to the unexpected links between their practices. By offering a fresh perspective on Calder and O’Keeffe’s little-known friendship, this exhibition takes its place alongside a series of presentations we’ve organized over the past 35 years, aimed at revealing new and previously unexplored pathways in the language of modernism and modern culture.

The book spans a critical decade in the couple’s marriage as well as a period of profound change and productivity in Guston’s artistic practice that saw the creation of some of his most iconic late works. A rich collection of artworks and archival images documents the couple’s domestic and social lives and the fellow artists and writers who made up their world. events.title: Radu Paponiu Conducts Concerto Competition Winners with the SFCM Orchestra
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerSan Francisco Symphony Youth Orchestra Music Director Radu Paponiu guides three SFCM student competition winners through the concertos of their choice.
Guitarist Kaz Hudson will be playing Mario Castelnuovo-Tedesco’s Guitar Concerto No. 1 in D Major, Op. 99; violinist Mark Chen Sergei Prokofiev’s Violin Concerto No. 1 in D Major, Op. 19; and cellist Lekai Li closes the evening with William Walton’s Cello Concerto.

SFCM’s annual Concerto Competition offers the student body the opportunity to star with the Conservatory Orchestra. This includes public orchestral workshops with distinguished guest conductors, like Donald Runnicles, Carl St. Clair, Nicola Luisotti, and Peter Oundjian.
Prior to his current role, Radu served as Associate Conductor of the Naples Philharmonic for five years, and seven as Music Director of the Philharmonic’s Youth Orchestra. He also served as Music Director for the Southwest Florida Symphony Orchestra, and has guested with symphony orchestras in San Francisco, Dallas, St. Louis, Rhode Island, Louisiana, Illinois, Colorado, and North Carolina. Aside from Naples, his international performances have included Berlin, Romania, Bologna, and Transylvania.
Presented by San Francisco Conservatory of Music

events.title: El Khat: Yemeni Junkyard Funk w/ DIY Instruments (Berkeley)
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerPresented by Hardly Strictly Bluegrass Festival’s “Out of the Park Series”
El Khat is a homemade junkyard band led by multi-instrumentalist Eyal El Wahab. Their original compositions are inspired by the music of the golden age in Aden, Yemen.

Experimenting with DIY, self-made instruments as an expression of a minimalist life philosophy—while remaining loyal to traditional Yemeni percussive roots—the three-piece developed a unique Arabic-Yemeni style. Although their detachment from any nation or flag is a driving force behind the group, the heart of their music and heritage remains deeply rooted in Yemeni culture. The constant divisions created by war and migration have given rise to a reassembled identity, one that resonates strongly throughout El Khat’s music. With a fourth album to be released in 2026, El Khat continues to forge a sound that bridges past and present—keeping Yemeni culture alive while reimagining its future.

events.description: Submitted by the Event OrganizerSinger and spoken-word artist Lisa B (Lisa Bernstein) celebrates the release or her 8th album, “’60s Magic Now!: The Y-Verse,” with her stellar band and special guests. After seven critically acclaimed records and a recent poetry book/audiobook with original music, Lisa presents a collection of stunning ’60s covers that are newly relevant today. Inspired by her ardent response to the repressive Trump administration, the album offers expressive new arrangements of various beloved ’60s tunes. Their more innocent calls for love and peace are infused with cutting-edge flavors — straightahead jazz, soul, funk, jazz-rock, hip-hop, and Latin. And Lisa’s new poetic raps reveal previously hidden rooms within many of the songs. The record spotlights four magical characters, each distinct figures of freedom: Spooky, Mr. Fantasy, Ruby Tuesday, and Windy. It includes two anthems from the time that passionately address social action: “The Times They Are A-Changin'” (Bob Dylan) and “Everybody Get Together” (the Youngbloods). Rounding out the evening are other songs from the ’60s or reminiscent of the decade from Lisa’s previous records:”What’s New, Pussycat?,” “Our House,” “What Is This Thing Called Love?,” “With Him and Max Roach’s Solo,” and various originals. Only 10 Miles from Gilroy! Mt. Madonna County Park is one of Santa Clara County’s most majestic regional park and recreation areas. The redwood forest dominates this 4,605-acre park, characteristic of the Santa Cruz Mountain range. To the east, the park overlooks the Santa Clara Valley, and to the west, Monterey Bay. events.title: The Green – Titles Tour 2026
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerFor over 15 years, The Green has been a cornerstone of the reggae music scene, seamlessly blending island roots with global appeal. Based in Hawaii, the band has become one of the most beloved and influential acts to emerge from the islands, pioneering U.S. mainland tours and sharing stages with reggae legends like Rebelution, Iration, SOJA, and Jamaica’s own Damian Marley. Their widespread acclaim caught the attention of Grammy-winning superstar Bruno Mars, who invited them to open for his sold-out shows at Honolulu’s Blaisdell Arena in 2014 and Hawaii’s iconic Aloha Stadium in 2018.
With themes of family, resilience, and unity woven into their music, The Green has cultivated a devoted global fanbase. Classics like “All I Need,” “Love I,” and “Wake Up” continue to resonate with long-time listeners, while collaborations with artists such as J Boog on tracks like “Feelings,” “Never Give Up,” and “Fire up Di Roses” draw in new audiences. Their recent single,Day by Day, featuring fellow Hawaii artist Kolohe Kai, celebrates the Aloha spirit and furthers their mission of spreading positivity.

events.description:
David Alvardo, Film director
Berkeley Public Library Presents
Film Screening : American Pachuco: The Legend of Luiz Valdez
Monday, October 5 | Berkeley Public Library, Central Branch, Community Meeting Room

Documentary about playwright and film director Luis Valdez. Film director David Alvarado will join on Zoom after the film screens to answer questions and describe working on the project.

Against political resistance and industry skepticism, Luis Valdez pushes Chicano storytelling from the fields to the film screen with Zoot Suit and La Bamba, crafting iconic works that challenge, celebrate, and expand America’s story.
Acclaimed playwright and director Luis Valdez recognized early on the profound impact of seeing one’s own humanity reflected onstage and on screen. He used theater to ignite change while working alongside farmworkers and Cesar Chavez, and he made films that amplified Chicano experiences. His work expanded audiences, bringing in people who had rarely seen their stories told before. Now, director David Alvarado reveals the fuel behind his legendary career.
Alvarado brings us close to Valdez, charting his career milestones and enduring cultural influence. He employs vibrant stylistic choices, using split screens, remarkable archival footage rescued from decay, and a pachuco narrator who tells it like it is by interjecting candid commentary throughout. events.title: Unfiltered Conversation: What Happened to the American Dream
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerCommon Wealth Club World Affairs​For generations, the American Dream has represented a promise of opportunity: work hard, and you can achieve economic stability, security, and upward mobility. Yet for many today, that promise feels uncertain—or fundamentally changed.
​Throughout our Dinner & Dialogue series, people across generations and backgrounds have gathered to share how they understand opportunity, success, and security in this moment. Now, we bring those insights to the stage.

​As the culminating event of this quarter’s Dinner & Dialogue series, What Happened to the American Dream?, this Unfiltered Conversation will bring together a panel of leading experts to respond directly to what emerged from those dialogues. Drawing on their expertise, lived perspectives, and disagreements, they’ll help us push the conversation further.
​The evening will unfold in two parts: a candid panel discussion, followed by an intergenerational dinner reception. Over dinner, participants will be grouped by age demographic and invited to reflect on what they’ve heard, exchange perspectives, and continue the dialogue with one another.
​Come hear what our community has learned, and put those insights in conversation with expert perspectives. Together, we’ll look beyond the white picket fence to ask: What has the American Dream been? What is it today? And what could it become?

events.title: Free String Quartet Concert w/ SF Ballet Orchestra Concertmaster
events.description:
San Francisco Conservatory of MusicViolinist Cordula Merks has been serving as Concertmaster of the San Francisco Ballet Orchestra since December 2015 after holding the Assistant Concertmaster position with the Seattle Symphony and Concertmaster roles with Germany’s Essen, Bochum, and Bergische symphony orchestras.
It’s no surprise then, that Merks’ Tomadachi Quartet-Mayumi Wyrick (violin), Amy Hiraga (viola), and Peter Wyrick (cello)-brings a high concentration of San Francisco talent to the Conservatory, with decades of experience across the Symphony and Ballet Orchestra among them.
Merks’ eclectic program seats contemporary vocal composer Caroline Shaw (Entr’acte, here arranged for string quartet) alongside George Gershwin (Lullaby) and stalwarts like Leos Janacek (String Quartet No. 2, Intimate Letters), and Antonin Dvorak (String Quartet No. 12 in F Major, Op. 96, American).

Janacek’s Intimate Letters is justly named: On a vacation, Janacek met and fell deeply in love Kamila Stosslova, undeterred by their 40-year age gap and the fact they were both married. For the next 11 years, Stosslova essentially functioned as Janacek’s muse: He wrote over 700 letters to her-and wrote four operas, two string quartets, a mass, and several orchestral works. Interestingly, most of their correspondence was suppressed by Czechoslovakia until 1990.
Dvorak’s American, one of the most popular string quartets in the canon, was written while the composer was vacationing in Spillville, Iowa,...

About Bota Tapas and Paella Bar

As an age-old tradition dating back to the early 1800s, Spanish travelers used “BOTA”, or traditional sheep-skinned repositories, to transport and share their wine. The Spaniards historically thrived on the values of sharing and community: two ideals that have buoyantly withstood the test of time. Tailored around these same ideals are Spain’s cuisine and the development of “tapas,” style dining – where individuals share small plates and memories. From Seville to San Francisco, and across the world, our goal is to initiate more memories – this is why and how we operate. Whether it be with your friends or family, we here at Bota sincerely hope that you enjoy this stop on your journey.

Submitted by the Event OrganizerFree Admission Day at Yerba Buena Center for the Arts (YBCA)
Yerba Buena Center for the Arts
Opened to the public in 1993, YBCA was founded as the cultural anchor of San Francisco’s Yerba Buena Gardens neighborhood. Our work spans the realms of contemporary art, performance, film, civic engagement, and public life. Centering artists as essential to social and cultural movement, YBCA is reimagining the role an arts institution can play in the community it serves.
YBCA is located in the heart of San Francisco’s SOMA neighborhood, across the street from SFMOMA and the Moscone Convention Center. The main entrance to our galleries and forum event space is at 701 Mission Street. The main entrance to our theater is 700 Howard Street.

YBCA is open Wednesday–Sunday, 11–5pm.

Free live music is back in the park.
Illuminate LIVE returns to the Golden Gate Bandshell in Golden Gate Park on Sunday, March 1, 2026, launching its sixth season of free outdoor concerts with more than 125 performances scheduled through mid-November.
The long-running series has quietly become one of San Francisco’s biggest free music traditions, drawing more than 250,000 attendees each year. After the afternoon sets, the 2026 season of Crucial Reggae Sundays launches with resident DJs Irie Dole, Guid8nce and DJ Sep.
2026 Season – March to Mid- November
The 2026 season features more than 125 free, all-ages performances, typically held:

Wednesdays – Midweek Melodies
Fridays – Friday Happy Hour
Sundays – Crucial Reggae Sundays
Plus select Saturdays and special cultural events

events.title: Conversation: On Archiving Punk
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerGoethe-Institut e.V. / PrivateWhat happens when a subculture becomes history? And who gets to preserve it?
Take a look inside the San Francisco Public Library’s Punk Archive and explore the stories, artifacts, and creative communities that shaped San Francisco’s punk history.

The evening offers a behind-the-scenes look at the archive as a growing, community-built collection, exploring how punk materials enter the archive, how provenance helps us understand their histories, and how archivists process, preserve, and make these collections accessible. The event also highlights the collaborative nature of punk archiving, including the important roles of donors and contributors, and what it means to care for fliers, photographs, and other ephemera from an underground cultural movement.
The event will feature Penelope Houston of the Avengers, who started the San Francisco Punk Archive with the support of the San Francisco Public Library, which holds key punk materials and ephemera; Freya Channing, archivist of the San Francisco Punk Archive and manager of the Little Maga/Zine Collection; and Christina Moretta, photo curator and manager of the San Francisco History Center at the San Francisco Public Library, the official archives for the City and County of San Francisco.

events.title: Free Public Talk on Finding Earth 2.0
events.address: 12345 El Monte Road, Los Altos Hills, CA
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerNASADr. Jessie Christiansen (CalTech) will give a free, illustrated, non-technical lecture entitled:
“The Search for Earth 2.0:

Why We Think It Exists, and How We’re Going to Find it ”
in the Smithwick Theater at Foothill College, in Los Altos (see directions below)
The talk is part of the Silicon Valley Astronomy Lecture Series, now in its 28th year.

For thousands of years, we’ve wondered if the Earth is unique, or if there are other Earths out there to find. In just the last 30 years, we’ve progressed from merely wondering if planets exist around other stars to knowing that almost every star we see has planets. Ambitious planet searches have been probing further and further, finding planetary systems of an incredible – and incredibly surprising! – variety. However, we have yet to discover another planet that might be like Earth – a rocky planet orbiting just the right distance from a Sun-like star to have liquid water on its surface. NASA has a audacious new plan for a next-generation flagship telescope that will directly image Earth-like planets around nearby stars, but it will take all of our ingenuity and technical prowess to achieve this feat. Dr Christiansen will walk you through the past, present, and future of our hunt for Earth 2.0.

events.title: Underground Labs: Kronos
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerKronos
Go behind the scenes with the Kronos Quartet as they rehearse new works and share a look at their creative process. In the process, Kronos has become one of the most celebrated and influential groups of our era, performing thousands of concerts worldwide, releasing more than 70 recordings of extraordinary breadth and creativity, and collaborating with many of the world’s most accomplished composers and performers. Through its nonprofit organization, Kronos Performing Arts Association (KPAA), Kronos has commissioned more than 1,100 works and arrangements for string quartet—including the recently completed 50 for the Future library of free, educational repertoire. Kronos has received more than 40 awards, including three Grammy Awards and the Polar Music, Avery Fisher, and Edison Klassiek Oeuvre Prizes—among the most prestigious awards given to musicians. In 2024, the Library of Congress announced its acquisition of the Archive of Kronos Quartet/Kronos Performing Arts Association, a collection that includes 50 years’ worth of manuscripts, instruments, costumes, video and audio recordings, photographs, and more.

events.title: District 9 Mission Family Summit
events.description:
San Francisco Department of Children, Youth & Their Families (DCYF)

This is Your City. This is Your Voice. This is Your Future. Share your story about growing up and raising your family in San Francisco.

Every family has a story. Every voice matters. Please share yours.
Join us for the District 9 Mission Family Summit! The This Is Your City: Family Summit Series invites families, caregivers, young people, and community members from across San Francisco to help shape the future of our city.

Thursday, Oct. 8, 2026, 5:00 p.m. – 7:30 p.m.
The Women’s Building, 3543 18th Street, SF, CA 94110

Free food, childcare, and interpretation are provided. Please note all interpretation requests must be made 48 hours or more prior to the Family Summit.
Who should attend? Everyone is welcome. This event highlights District 9, but you can attend any Family Summit that fits your schedule.
Why are we gathering? The Family Summit Series is part of San Francisco’s first Citywide Community Needs Assessment. Through conversations with families across the city, we’re learning what matters most to children, youth, young adults, and families. Penguin Random HouseKPFA co-presents this evening celebrating the publication of The People’s Historian: The Outsized Life of Howard Zinn, by Dave Zirin, a columnist at The Nation.
​The new book examines the life and work of the iconic radical historian Howard Zinn, whose bestselling work, A People’s History of the United States, changed the way Americans saw the past.

events.title: Dying Fetus and Sanguisugabogg
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerThe UC TheatreDying Fetus
DYING FETUS established a reputation for uncompromising integrity with a slew of classic albums and today rides a resurgence of respect and esteem with a new generation. As Revolver Magazine wrote upon the release of their first new material since 2017’s Wrong One To Fuck With: “Their unique sound has always straddled the line between extreme metal instrumentation and heavy hardcore chugginess, and right now, they’re extremely well-regarded by many of today’s heavy-hitting hardcore acts, as well as their fair share of death metal and deathcore up-and-comers.”

Sanguisugabogg
Shat out of hell, indeed. That’s the sonic stench that permeates the epically unpronounceable, utterly indecipherable and altogether uncompromising sound of Ohio’s notorious gore-merchants, SANGUISUGABOGG. Homicidal Ecstasy, the ‘Bogg’s second Century Media platter of splatter isn’t merely a return to the “down-tuned drug death” that defined 2021’s Tortured Whole. It’s the fluid-streaked byproduct of a band that hit the road like crazed serial killers and never looked back as they plunged deeper into a celebration of Mortician-worshiping brutal death metal sounds and splatter classics like Dead-Alive. They also became a badass live and studio proposition in the process.

events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerThe Other Minds Festival turns 30! On Thursday–Sunday, October 8–11, 2026, our annual showcase for composers will be held at the Brava Theater in San Francisco’s Mission District.
The Festival opens with Joseph Bohigian’s I Am He Whose Life and Soul Are Torment, an evening-length multimedia work about the life of the visionary Soviet-Armenian film director Sergei Parajanov (1924–1990) that combines the multilingual songs of the 18th century bard Sayat Nova in Armenian, Azeri, and Georgian with live electronic manipulation of recordings by South Caucasus folk musicians. A collaboration with vocalist and duduk player Khatchadour Khatchadourian, Ensemble Decipher, and artists Tara Baghdassarian and Karo Yagjian, the piece is written for solo voice, duduk, electronics ensemble, and video projection.

On Night 2, the Swiss-born, New York-based Sylvie Courvoisier combines European chamber music and American avant-jazz in a performance for solo piano. Mahsa Vahdat performs original song settings of Persian poetry, accompanied by setar player Atabak Elyasi. Vahdat’s compositions are inspired by her life in exile, her deep belonging to her homeland of Iran, and her dedication to preserving and reviving Iranian music. Night 2 ends with Juri Seo’s Just Intonation Etudes and Wildflowers followed by the world premiere of her Bad Decision for string quartet, bass, and drumset, with Friction Quartet.

events.title: Odyssea
events.address: 9th and Lincoln Street, San Francisco, CA
events.description: Submitted by the Event OrganizerWe PlayersMeet CASEMA: The Conference Attending Society of Eleusinian Mystery Appreciators! A self-styled secret society, these massive fans of classical antiquity pose as hotel service workers in order to sneak into academic conferences and in this way be close to their erudite heroes and absorb some essence of their Olympic-level intellectual prowess. Our characters make the ancient myths their own through unique interpretations and stitch themselves into the lineage of homeric bards through telling their versions of the tales. Bringing themselves joy by taking it all very seriously and savoring silliness, these clowns know that like the Gods themselves we can be both sacred and ridiculous, solemn and irreverent, agnostic and devoted, petty and sincere, all at once. Perhaps this is the truth the Gods represent, that the Divine is all things, in all places, at all times, all at once.

Japanese Tea Garden
The Japanese Tea Garden provides visitors from around the world with an opportunity to experience the natural beauty, tranquility, and harmony of a Japanese-style garden in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park.
Originally created as a “Japanese Village” exhibit for the 1894 California Midwinter International Exposition, the Japanese Tea Garden endures as one of the most popular attractions in San Francisco, featuring classic elements such as an arched drum bridge, pagodas, stone lanterns, stepping stone paths, native Japanese plants, serene koi ponds, and a zen garden. Cherry blossom trees bloom throughout the garden in March and April.
Admission to the Japanese Tea Garden is free for San Francisco residents with valid ID. Free hours for everyone (even non-residents) are 9-10 am every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

events.title: SPAM New Media Festival (Santa Cruz)
events.description:
Design: Wyatt OlsonSPAM New Media Festival began in 2022 as a grassroots experimental arts platform, bringing together practitioners working on the fringes and frontiers of digital arts through exhibitions, performances, and critical discussions.
SPAM’s organizers and curators are a collective of artists, researchers, and academics who are bugging the system — imagining resistance narratives against capital-driven media through multiplicity, embodiment, and critical practice.
For SPAM’s 2026 iteration we’re gathering October 9–11, 2026, at Indexical in Santa Cruz, CA to share the work of artists we love with the greater San Francisco Bay Area community through performances, workshops, and artist talks.
The 2026 lineup features regional projects by Dorothy Santos & Abram Stern, Ava Koohbor, Jean Carla Rodea, and EPOCH, alongside the touring projects of Sunken Cages and Rohan Chander.
SPAM 2026 is organized in collaboration with Indexical and SrcMaterial. Indexical is generously hosting the event, supporting the performances, and creating a space for gathering and relationality. SrcMaterial is curating Allaboration, a workshop series focused on technological literacy — with an emphasis on AI, collaboration, and connection in an era of increasingly asynchronous workspaces.
SPAM is an ongoing project of regrowth and persistence. We are committed to creating discourse from the margins, developing pathways of interconnectivity for our future selves.

events.title: Slow-Paced Golden Gate Park Ride w/ Adaptive Bikes
events.address: 75 Hagiwara Tea Garden Dr, San Francisco, CA
events.description:
BORP Adaptive Sports and RecreationSan Francisco shines in October! Let’s spend some time outside together and explore Golden Gate Park on wheels. San Francisco Village, BORP Adaptive Sports and Recreation, and the San Francisco Bicycle Coalition are partnering to bring together riders of all ages and will have bikes to available to meet your accessibility needs. This ride is perfect for elders, families with kids, and anyone who would like to enjoy the park on a beautiful Friday afternoon.
Let us know what would help you join us – BORP will provide recumbent electric assist bikes, tandem side by side bikes, bikes with recumbent seats, and more! If you have a body, we’ll do our best to find a bike with the right fit/support. If you are borrowing an accessible bike, plan to get to the Bandshell by 2:00 PM to sign a waiver and find the right fit. If you want to partner with someone to help them ride, let us know and come by 2:00 PM.
You are also welcome to bring and ride your own bike! The pace will be slow and conversational and we don’t drop anyone. The route can be found at https://ridewithgps.com/routes/56763052. Organizers request you wear a helmet as well; BORP will have some available for those using an accessible bike.

In this show, Lara Aburamadan explores the transformation of memories of home shaped by the relentless impact of war, transitioning from tangible reality to the ethereal realms of daydreams and nostalgia. Having lived in exile for years, Aburamadan is left pondering the uncertain path ahead, questioning the fate of a Gaza that clings to memories of people and places that don’t exist anymore.

REMAINS A MEMORY FILM
“Experience the essence of Gaza in ‘Remains a Memory, a short documentary captured in seven-second vines spanning 2014 to 2016. Filmed from the artist’s balcony, now obliterated, the sea, fishermen, farmers, food, nightscapes, changing seasons, and the poignant borders and streets, these glimpses into daily life, the aftermath of the 2014 war, are a visual journey into the heart of a homeland forever altered. With each fleeting scene, the artist invites you to witness the warmth and nostalgia that bursts forth from her memories. As Gaza stands transformed, these seven-second clips become a testament to resilience and an ode to a time when life persisted against the backdrop of destruction, now eternally etched in the artist’s evocative recollections.”

events.title: Yerba Buena Illuminated: Free 95-Ft Art Projection on Market Street
events.description:
Yerba Buena Illuminated: Free 95-Ft Art Projection on Market Street
Yerba Buena Partnership
San Francisco has officially turned a downtown building into a giant art projector.

Yerba Buena Illuminated launched Tuesday, August 25, 2026 projecting giant digital artworks onto the historic Humboldt Bank Building at 785 Market St., at the top of Yerba Buena Lane. The massive projection covers a 95-foot-high by 46-foot-wide section of the building, turning one of Market Street’s historic facades into a giant outdoor art screen.

The free outdoor art show runs nightly from twilight until 10 p.m., with the first artwork on view for about 90 days. The inaugural projection is Jennifer Steinkamp’s It’s a nice day for a white wedding. (2008), from SFMOMA’s collection. Inspired by Billy Idol’s “White Wedding,” the digital artwork covers the Beaux-Arts-style building with a cascade of animated red, white and yellow wedding flowers.

The project is a collaboration between Yerba Buena Partnership, SFMOMA, the Museum of the African Diaspora and Yerba Buena Center for the Arts. And this first installation is just the beginning: MoAD and YBCA will curate future projections in 2027, so the giant building-as-canvas is sticking around.
The projection is designed to serve as a giant welcome sign for the Yerba Buena arts district, home to more than 60 public artworks and some of San Francisco’s biggest cultural institutions. The rotating projections will continue to light up the Humboldt Bank Buildi...

events.title: Step Into Wonder – Deep Dive Workshop
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerPriscila Soares

Go beyond the surface of creativity with Step Into Wonder: Deep Dive, an intimate, guided art experience for adults at Mare Island Art Studios.
Led by artist Priscila Soares, this three-hour session uses art-making, creative prompts and reflection to explore what happens when we quiet the inner critic, let go of expectations and give ourselves permission to create freely.

No artistic experience is needed. The focus isn’t on making something “good”—it’s on curiosity, expression and discovering what can emerge when you stop trying to control the outcome.
Set within the immersive Step Into Wonder installation, surrounded by glowing sculptures and a transformed gallery environment, the Deep Dive offers a smaller, more intentional experience for those who want to explore the deeper side of The Letting Go Art Experience.
Come as you are. Get messy. Follow your intuition. See what happens when you let go.
October 10 & 24 • 10 AM–1 PM18+ • $45 • Limited to 15 participantsMare Island Art Studios, 110 Pintado St., Vallejo

events.description:
© Out There WatercolorsFree outdoor painting gathering at the Palace of Fine Arts.
Come paint with us. Sign up at Painters Unite to hear about future gatherings.
Painters Unite is a free gathering for anyone who wants to slow down and paint outdoors, together. No class, no pressure, nothing for sale.
I’m Marco Flavio, a watercolor teacher here in the city. I started this because so many people told me they wanted more time to paint and to be around others, and I think that shouldn’t have to cost anything. I’ll be painting right alongside you, same as everyone.

This time we’re meeting at the Palace of Fine Arts, at the intersection of Baker Street and Beach Street at 10AM. From there we’ll have a beautiful view across the lagoon toward the Palace, with the architecture, water, and reflections all in front of us. It’s a great opportunity to play with reflections in watercolor and simplify a pretty spectacular scene into a painting.
As always, I’ll bring a few small challenges, different ways of seeing and painting what’s in front of us. I’ll also have a limited number of pre-drawings of the Palace of Fine Arts on watercolor paper, first come, first served, for beginners who’d like a starting point. Take a challenge, use a pre-draw, or simply find a spot and paint. No experience needed.

events.description:
Melissa LaiLawton Alternative School’s Fall Fest is bringing a burst of creativity to the Sunset, and it’s free to attend. On Saturday, October 10, 2026, families can enjoy an afternoon of community fun featuring local food vendors, plus a one‑of‑a‑kind arcade inspired by Caine’s Arcade. Every carnival-style game has been imagined and hand-built by Lawton’s 5th graders using recycled and repurposed materials — turning cardboard, tape, and everyday items into something truly magical.
Visitors can play the student‑made games, meet the young creators behind them, and experience a project that celebrates imagination, teamwork, and creativity. Admission is free, and game play and food are available for purchase, with proceeds supporting the 5th graders’ graduation festivities.
If you’re looking for a feel‑good, family‑friendly event that showcases kids building something extraordinary for their community, Fall Fest is a perfect weekend pick.

events.title: Second Saturdays ‘Round the World at Union Square: Bollywood Garba
events.address: Geary and Powell, San Francisco, CA
events.description:
Rang De BollywoodJoin us for our final Second Saturdays ‘Round the World event this year at Union Square! Get ready to twirl in an unforgettable Bollywood Garba at the heart of San Francisco — a vibrant celebration of rhythm, joy, and community in the festive season of Navratri.
Second Saturdays ‘Round the World
Saturday, October 10, 2026 | 11a – 2p
Union Square Park, Geary and Powell, SF
FREE
Schedule:

11:00 am – 1:00 pm: Bolly Garba Dance Lessons. No experience needed, we’ll teach you the steps, the flair, and the fun!
1:00 pm – 2:00 pm: Dance Party! We turn up the music and light up the floor with a 1-hour open dance party. Dance solo, with friends, or in circles of celebration!

Expect a fusion of traditional Garba beats and Bollywood bangers, colorful, energetic, and full of heart. Its non-stop fun entertainment! You won’t want to stop dancing.
Open to all ages, all levels, all backgrounds. Wear your brightest, twirliest outfits or come as you are. Free to attend, just bring your joy, your people, and your dancing feet!
Come casual or dressed. No pressure. Beginner friendly. Walk ins and people who have never done Garba (a circular Indian dance) more than welcome. We will do multiple lessons throughout the day and have performances party after each lesson.
Dress as you want Indian or Non-Indian, no pressure, be comfortable. Let’s fill Union Square with color, culture, and connection. This is more than a dance, it’s a celebration of culture, community, and love.

events.title: Bridging The Gap: An Evening of Indian Music
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerNazan Aktaswith Nazan Aktas (Cello) & William Rossel (Tabla)
​Nazan Aktas (cello) & William Rossel (tabla) will present a performance of afternoon and evening ragas in the styles of the North Indian, Maihar and Lucknow gharanas. This performance will highlight the versatility of the cello and tabla as both solo and accompanying instruments, as each player will take turns accompanying the other. The cello (being a relatively new instrument to Indian music) and tabla together will bridge the gap between old & new in the hopes of sharing the beautiful music of the North Indian Classical tradition.
​In Person Only at the SF Dharma Collective, 2929 24th Street.

​Nazan Aktas is a cellist based in Northern California who has performed with many artists, ensembles and orchestras throughout the Bay Area and beyond. She has been studying at the Ali Akbar College of Music since 2015, under the tutelage of Alam Khan, son of Maestro Ali Akbar Khan. She has also studied vocal music with Ranjana Ghatak, disciple of Pandit Ajoy Chakraborty and received further instruction from cellist Saskia Rao-de Haas, who studied with Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia. She is a graduate of Sonoma State University, with a Bachelor of Music Degree with a double concentration in Performance and Jazz Studies and has a Master’s Degree from Berklee College of Music in Contemporary Performance.

events.title: Litquake: Claudia Rankine: Triage
events.description:
Submitted by the Event Organizer

The award-winning author of Citizen: An American Lyric returns with a new genre-defying work blending essay, memoir, and visual art

Sponsored by Alta Journal

Poet Claudia Rankine’s work is unfailingly expansive—broadening readers’ understanding of race, social conscience, and the limits of genre. Triage, Rankine’s first book since the groundbreaking “American” trilogy (whose centerpiece, Citizen, was a 2023 Alta California Book Club selection), is another boundary-defying work. Here Rankine traces a decades-long friendship between two women—the narrator and the theorist—following their evolving relationship against the background of ever-more-turbulent times.
In an uncategorizable mix of essay, criticism, memoir, and photography, Rankine creates a politically urgent book that Booklist calls “Startlingly original … A remarkable, soul-stirring work.” Joining Rankine in conversation is Cathy Park Hong, whose award-winning nonfiction book Minor Feelings engages intimately with Rankine’s ideas. The Alta Journal team will be on hand to introduce you to upcoming California Book Club selections, and we’ll kick things off with performances by 2026 Oakland Youth Poet Laureate Isaiah Kahn and Vice OYPL Isabel Shen. Doors at 6:30pm.

events.title: “Welcome Back Monarch” Butterfly Festival 2026 (Santa Cruz)
events.address: 2531 W Cliff Dr, Santa Cruz, CA 95060
events.description:
Santa Cruz State BeachesWelcome Back Monarch Festival is a free family event at Natural Bridges State Beach featuring crafts, hands-on learning, a parade, story time, games, live music, food trucks, hand-cranked pumpkin ice cream, and items for sale. The 2026 festival also includes a screening of “Creating the West Marin Monarch Sanctuary,” a monarch photo exhibit by Elizabeth Weber, and a talk by Julia Butterfly Hill. Free cake is listed on the event flyer; parking costs $10.
The Monarchs return every year around mid October and typically stay for 3-4 months.
Every fall and winter, Natural Bridges State Beach welcomes back the monarchs to their winter habitat in the eucalyptus grove, the only State Monarch Preserve in California. Starting in early to mid-October, the black and orange beauties start trickling in from colder climates to enjoy our moderate coastal weather. Scientifically speaking, monarchs are tropical butterflies and at no point in their life cycle – egg, caterpillar, chrysalis, butterfly – can they freeze, so they move with the warmer weather while migrating south.

Natural Bridges State Beach is California’s only state park designated as a monarch preserve, featuring a protected canyon eucalyptus grove and an accessible 0.4-mile trail.

events.title: SF’s Annual Italian Heritage Festival & Parade 2026
events.address: Jefferson and Taylor, San Francisco, CA
events.description:
Italian Heritage Festival & ParadeThe San Francisco Italian Heritage Parade returns to the streets of San Francisco on Sunday, October 11, 2026, bringing Italian-American culture, music, performances, floats, and community groups to the streets of North Beach.
The San Francisco Italian Heritage Parade is the longest continuously running Italian Heritage Parade in the United States and celebrates the accomplishments and culture of Italian-Americans. The inaugural parade took place in 1868 in downtown San Francisco, featuring bands and marching units from Italian fraternal organizations. Throughout the years, the parade has remained a celebration of the vitality of Italian communities throughout the Bay Area.
Parade Route
The parade begins at 12:30 p.m. at the foot of Jefferson and Powell Streets in Fisherman’s Wharf, then proceeds through North Beach along Columbus Avenue before ending in Washington Square in front of Saints Peter and Paul Church. Parade viewing is available throughout the entire route.

The celebration features Italian and Italian-American dignitaries, live Italian music, performances, floats, and representatives from Italian and Italian-American organizations and businesses. Admission is free.

David Cay Johnston has covered Trump longer and more closely than any other journalist working today, his many books include, The Big Cheat: How Donald Trump Fleeced America and Enriched Himself and His Family (2021), It’s Even Worse Than You Think: What the Trump Administration Is Doing to America (2019) and The Making of Donald Trump (2017).

Ian Masters hosts, Background Briefing on KPFA and KPFK which deals with American politics, foreign policy as well as domestic American security issues. It is broadcast on more than forty radio stations across the US, and is also available as a podcast. Masters is an Australian-born, BBC-trained American broadcast journalist, commentator, author screenwriter and documentary filmmaker.

Submitted by the Event OrganizerAndrea Prichett & FriendsIn an evening with Andrea Prichett and Friends, you can expect to be taken on something of a journey. From tender ballads to raucous political anthems, the performance moves between the personal and the political and sometimes both at the same time.
The rich resonance of Andrea’s voice carries the message of her original lyrics on a versatile instrumental foundation provided by Deborah Hungerford on piano and keyboards, Mike Derrick on guitar, and Alexis Tsamoudakis on bass. The genre defying tunes range from blues, folk, rock and even jazz at times. While Andrea’s influences include singer-songwriters (Patti Griffin, Tracy Chapman, Joni Mitchell, James Taylor, etc), she also loves to dance and so the R&B/Motown sound is also woven into the mix.

Formerly of the Berkeley-based, nationally-known feminist folk trio Rebecca Riots, Andrea has released several albums. In recent times, Andrea released a solo album, The Frame, and continues to write and sing about the issues of the day. A natural storyteller and political activist, Andrea combines anecdotes with her carefully crafted songs to inspire and uplift her audiences. Her fans describe the experience of going to her shows as part political, part spiritual, part humorous and TOTALLY engaging!

events.title: SF’s “Circus By The Bay” Night: History Panel + Wild Live Acts (Fort Mason)
events.description:
Fort Mason Center for Arts & CultureCowell Theater hosts a panel conversation and live performances exploring San Francisco’s new American circus movement. Pickle Family Circus and New Pickle Circus veterans Gypsy Snider, Shana Carroll, Jeff Raz, and Tandy Beal will discuss the scene’s history, alongside archival photos and video and performances by artists from Prescott Circus, Dear San Francisco, Circus Bella, and San Francisco Youth Circus.
Original Event Description:
CIRCUS BY THE BAY
Panel conversation and live performances
Tuesday, October 13, 2026 – 7:00 p.m. to 8:30 p.m.
Cowell Theater, Pier 2/Gateway Pavilion, FMCAC, RESERVE SPACE
In the 1970s, San Francisco became an epicenter of the emerging new American circus – an intimate one-ring model that spurned animal acts and focused on traditional skills of juggling, clowning, acrobatics, and aerial work, all filtered through a countercultural vaudevillian sensibility. This “not-so-big-top” was pioneered by such local companies as the Pickle Family Circus and its later incarnation, the New Pickle Circus, which performed annually at Fort Mason Center For Arts & Culture, and longtime FMCAC residents Make*A*Circus. This movement spawned a stream of Bay Area talents that spread their influence from Cirque du Soleil and Broadway to movies, and TV, an impact which resonates to this day.

events.title: The Science Scoop: Women’s Health Breakthroughs w/ UCSF Professor
events.description:
UCSFThe Science Scoop
Please join us for the next session of The Science Scoop, a quarterly public lecture series hosted by UCSF Basic Sciences. Discovery for ALL!
We invite you to learn about how curiosity-driven research is leading to critical medical advances. Through engaging lectures geared towards a lay audience, premier researchers at the University of California, San Francisco will share the challenges and joys of making scientific discoveries and their impact on bettering human health. The audience will have the opportunity to ask questions at the end of the talk.
This is a FREE lecture open to the general public, and all are welcome. No tickets or registration needed.

The Speaker
Holly A. Ingraham, PhD, is the Herzstein Professor of Molecular Physiology at the University of California, San Francisco. Her research focuses on hormone-responsive nodes in the brain and peripheral tissues that impact metabolic, skeletal, and gut physiology and women’s health. Through question-driven basic science, Ingraham has uncovered how hormonal fluctuations lead to adaptive responses in females across their lifespan. Ingraham is an elected fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science and a member of the National Academy of Sciences and the American Academy of Arts and Sciences. She earned her Ph.D. from UCSD.
https://ingrahamlab.ucsf.edu/

events.title: Conversation: (Un)Writing Place
events.description:
Submitted by the Event Organizer© privateJoin us for a lively conversation between author and journalist Lin Hierse and translator-scholar Dr. Jon Cho-Polizzi. Hierse’s writing navigates the complexities of life in contemporary Germany, exploring links between language, place, and belonging across generations. Her works are characterized by complex ambiguities, settings and narratives that compound and merge, demonstrating unexpected connections and continuities. Together they will discuss Hierse‘s explorations of German and Chinese entanglements in her writing, the role of Chinatowns across the diaspora, and the publication of her works in English translation in new and forthcoming anthologies.
Lin Hierse

Lin Hierse is a prolific author, journalist, poet, and public intellectual. With a background in Asian Studies and Human Geography, she is a longtime contributor to several major German journals and periodicals; she wrote the biweekly column “Poetical Correctness” in taz from 2020-2023. The Japanese Tea Garden provides visitors from around the world with an opportunity to experience the natural beauty, tranquility, and harmony of a Japanese-style garden in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park.

events.title: Glaive – God Save the Three Tour
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerThe UC TheatreFrom his beginnings in Hendersonville, North Carolina (population 15k), to opening for The Kid LAROI on The First Time tour last year, glaive has become a name synonymous with a scene that redefines pop, not by distancing itself from tradition but by forging a new, innovative style. His previous works, including cypress grove, all dogs go to heaven, and then i’ll be happy, have all cemented him as a standout artist, lauded by the likes of The New York Times, Vulture, GQ and The FADER.

His 2nd studio album released in late 2024, May It Never Falter, was hailed as a genre-defying body of work that marked the beginning of an independent chapter in his artistry. Working closely with a tight-knit team of collaborators including John Cunningham (XXXTENTACION, Kanye West), Ralph Castelli (Dora Jar, The Neighbourhood), and Jeff Hazin (Kali Uchis, renforshort) the album served as a coming-of-age narrative set against the backdrop of adolescence and self-discovery. May It Never Falter was recorded in the remote landscapes of Iceland and Wales, continuing the Sigur Rós-inspired approach to isolated, immersive recording environments that began with his debut album i care so much i don’t care at all (2023). The album was listed as one of the best of 2024 by Vogue Magazine and was supported by a North American and European tour in spring of 2025.

events.title: Yerba Buena Illuminated: Free 95-Ft Art Projection on Market Street
events.description:
Yerba Buena Illuminated: Free 95-Ft Art Projection on Market Street
Yerba Buena Partnership
San Francisco has officially turned a downtown building into a giant art projector.

Yerba Buena Illuminated launched Tuesday, August 25, 2026 projecting giant digital artworks onto the historic Humboldt Bank Building at 785 Market St., at the top of Yerba Buena Lane. The massive projection covers a 95-foot-high by 46-foot-wide section of the building, turning one of Market Street’s historic facades into a giant outdoor art screen.

The free outdoor art show runs nightly from twilight until 10 p.m., with the first artwork on view for about 90 days. The inaugural projection is Jennifer Steinkamp’s It’s a nice day for a white wedding. (2008), from SFMOMA’s collection. Inspired by Billy Idol’s “White Wedding,” the digital artwork covers the Beaux-Arts-style building with a cascade of animated red, white and yellow wedding flowers.

The project is a collaboration between Yerba Buena Partnership, SFMOMA, the Museum of the African Diaspora and Yerba Buena Center for the Arts. And this first installation is just the beginning: MoAD and YBCA will curate future projections in 2027, so the giant building-as-canvas is sticking around.

Submitted by the Event OrganizerjwBECAUSE I HAVE TO is a discussion series featuring Bay Area artists, writers, musicians, chefs, and creators who work across multiple artistic and creative mediums, against the grain of their professional lives, alongside it, or within it. Hosted by Jeff Wright, these conversations will delve into creative work in the modern age, the real whys that drive us to make it, how it intertwines with our lives, and what really makes it all possible.

BIHT #1 will feature Amar Lal and Paolo Bicchieri. If you’re in the Bay Area, their fingerprints are probably already on something familiar to you, due to their presence and commitment to culture and creative work here. Professionally, Amar is fine-tuning and refining songs we listen to at his Oakland studio every day. He also creates visual works of art to express sound, as noted in his latest book, Practicing Joy. Paolo’s creative writing can be found in any given news outlet, narrating underrepresented projects, or throughout his handful of published poetry works. He also organizes community events to uplift local poets, writers, and up-and-coming chefs through Kitchen Table. All of this work takes perseverance, the right settings, creative discipline, and much more that we are set to discuss in the first edition of BECAUSE I HAVE TO.

berkeleybirdfestival.org

Free | Family-Friendly | All Ages
Every bird holds a memory. Every memory holds a meaning. Across different cultures and communities, across time and space, birds have played a significant role in shaping our understanding of the world, ourselves, and our relationship in nature.
On Sunday, October 18th, this year’s Berkeley Bird Festival invites you to celebrate our incredible birdlife here in the Bay Area through the theme of “Myth and Memories”.
Get outside and witness the birds and our shared environment. Engage with the Myth of the Flying Africans. Fold a crane for peace and longevity. Hear the story of SF’s Wild Parrots. Watch the street “split the sky” through a dance inspired by migration. Listen to the science behind wildlife and remember, every feather, past and present, is a portal to a world where all of us thrive.
This festival brings science, art, and culture under its wing to inspire our collective imagination and action in protecting birds and our environment. We hope you’ll join us whether you’re bird-curious or a long-time advocate.
Register in advance to attend a trip, or gather your flock, swoop in, and dive into a world of birds, Myth and Memory.

Japanese Tea Garden
The Japanese Tea Garden provides visitors from around the world with an opportunity to experience the natural beauty, tranquility, and harmony of a Japanese-style garden in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park.
Originally created as a “Japanese Village” exhibit for the 1894 California Midwinter International Exposition, the Japanese Tea Garden endures as one of the most popular attractions in San Francisco, featuring classic elements such as an arched drum bridge, pagodas, stone lanterns, stepping stone paths, native Japanese plants, serene koi ponds, and a zen garden. Cherry blossom trees bloom throughout the garden in March and April.
Admission to the Japanese Tea Garden is free for San Francisco residents with valid ID. Free hours for everyone (even non-residents) are 9-10 am every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

The Bawdy Caste performs a full shadow cast of The Rocky Horror Picture Show, acting out the movie in front of the screen while it plays with audience participation. events.title: Bat Week Screening of ‘The Invisible Mammal’
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerThe Invisible Mammal

Award-winning documentary highlights global bat extinction crisis

The Citizens Environmental Council invites you to a free screening of an award-winning documentary highlighting the fight to save North American bats on Wednesday, October 21, from 6 to 8 p.m. at the Burlingame Community Center at 850 Burlingame Ave. in Burlingame. There is no charge for admission, but pre-registration is required. Watch the trailer below!

Just in time for Halloween – and Bat Week! – “The Invisible Mammal” focuses on the plight of several species of North American bats now at risk because of a deadly fungal disease called White-nose Syndrome (WNS) and a team of women biologists determined to rescue these rapidly vanishing species. After a screening of the 90-minute film, filmmaker Kristin Tièche will offer insights and answer questions about a strategy called Operation Fat Bat, pioneered by women scientists, that could rebuild healthy bat populations across North America.
Bats save U.S. agriculture billions of dollars in pesticide use each year, and the decline of bat populations is linked to an increase in infant mortality where these pesticides are used. Since 2006, WNS has decimated bat populations across 42 states and Canada, killing millions of bats.
